key_insight: A two-stage tuning pipeline—offline CMA-ES plus circuit-aware ranking—can automatically select better MPS simulator hyperparameters than defaults for many quantum circuits.
engineering_relevance: For quantum simulation workflows, this offers a practical way to reduce runtime and improve fidelity by matching MPS settings to circuit structure instead of relying on fixed defaults.
method: Stage 1: run offline single-objective CMA-ES optimization with a fidelity constraint to build a circuit–configuration–performance database.
Stage 2: extract static circuit features that reflect MPS-relevant structure and train a hybrid ranking model to recommend configurations.
Validate on scalable circuit families using leave-one-family-out and size-based splits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that offline optimization often beats default settings, and the learned predictor recovers a meaningful fraction of that gain, especially under size-based validation.
watch_item: Generalization is weaker across circuit families than across sizes, so recommendations may transfer poorly to unseen circuit types or backends.
